articles.title: What is Connect2Minds?
articles.answer: Connect2Minds helps students and professionals find the right people, build projects in teams and keep up with college. You can discover people by skill, chat and call, plan projects in Project Hub, use College Hub with your teachers, and track your studies in My Study.

articles.title: Create an account
articles.answer: Press Sign up and fill four short steps: your account, your college background, your college ID (optional, it gets you verified faster) and your profile. A college email ending in .edu.in or .ac.in is verified straight away.

articles.title: Log in
articles.answer: Log in with your roll number (or ID) and your password on the Log in page. Tick “Keep me logged in” to stay logged in for 30 days; leave it off on a shared computer and you are logged out when the browser closes. If you asked to delete your account in the last 14 days, logging in cancels the deletion.

articles.title: I forgot my password
articles.answer: Press “Forgot password?” on the Log in page and type your roll number, ID or email. We email a link that works once for 30 minutes; choosing a new password logs out every other device. If your account has no email or nothing arrives, write to Support with your roll number and the team can send you a link.

highlight.text: Type your roll number, ID or email here.

articles.title: Getting verified
articles.answer: Your account is checked by an admin for your college department. Add or replace your college ID card from your own profile; if the admin asks a question you will see it there. Verified people get a tick on their card.

highlight.text: Your verification status, with a button to send a new ID photo when an admin asks for one.

articles.title: Home: what needs you today
articles.answer: Home collects what needs you: unread messages, College Hub work and polls, classes today, opportunities that ask for your skills, people you may know and your week. The checklist at the end helps you finish setting up.

highlight.text: Things waiting for you right now.
Opportunities that ask for your skills.

articles.title: Phone and desktop notifications
articles.answer: The bell at the top shows your notifications. To get them even when the site is closed, switch on notifications from Home; your browser will ask for permission. Logging out stops them on that device.

highlight.text: Notification and email switches are here on Home.

articles.title: Weekly summary email
articles.answer: Connect2Minds can send a short weekly email of what happened. Switch it on or off on Home; every email also has a link to stop it.

articles.title: Find people by skill (Discover)
articles.answer: Discover lists everyone on the site. Search by name, skill, college or project, filter by college, department, city or type, then follow, save or message people. Cards show skills you have in common.

highlight.text: Type a skill like React or a name.
Narrow by college, department or city.

articles.title: Professionals by profession
articles.answer: Professionals groups people by field and profession, with what they are open to (mentoring, hiring, internships…) and their experience. Pick a field, then a profession, and introduce yourself with a short message.

highlight.text: Start by choosing a field.

articles.title: Advanced filters (paid)
articles.answer: On Professionals, needing two or more skills at once, the “open to” filter and sorting by experience are part of Student Pro and the Premium plans. Everything else is free.

articles.title: Opportunities board
articles.answer: The Opportunities board lists open roles and project ideas. Filter by category or skill, apply with a short note, or post your own. Urgent posts are shown first, and sponsored challenges and hackathons appear here too.

highlight.text: Pick a category.
Search posts by skill or title.

articles.title: Post an opportunity
articles.answer: On the Opportunities board press the button to post, choose a category, give a title, the skills you need and a description. People who apply show up under your post's applicants.

articles.title: Sponsored challenges and hackathons
articles.answer: Sponsored challenges and hackathons are posted on the Opportunities board with a prize and deadline. Open one, submit your entry link (alone or as a team) before the deadline, and winners are announced on the post.

articles.title: Campus Network
articles.answer: Campus Network shows everyone who studies at your college, by department, with who is online. Invite classmates with the invite button.

highlight.text: Switch between departments.
Invite classmates.

articles.title: Followers and following
articles.answer: My Network shows who follows you, who you follow and mutual follows, plus suggested people. Follow anyone from their card; following someone who follows you makes messaging free of limits.

highlight.text: Followers, following and mutual.

articles.title: Saved profiles
articles.answer: Save people from their card to find them later in Saved Profiles. You can select several and add them to a team in one go.

articles.title: Your profile
articles.answer: Open your profile from the picture at the top right. Edit your bio, skills, college details, profession and what you are open to; change your picture and banner; add projects and your GitHub; copy your profile link to share.

highlight.text: Edit your profile from here.

articles.title: Show your projects
articles.answer: On your profile add projects with a title, description, tech stack, GitHub and live links and a picture. Linking your GitHub username shows your public repositories and stars.

highlight.text: Add a project here.

articles.title: Messages
articles.answer: Messages has one-to-one chats, a Professionals section for chats started from that page, and Groups for your teams. You can send files, voice notes, code snippets and emoji, search inside a chat and see read ticks.

highlight.text: Start a new chat.
Your one-to-one chats.

articles.title: Message limits on the free plan
articles.answer: On the free plan you can start a limited number of new conversations each month with people who don't follow you. Replies, people who follow you and chats you already have are always free; paid plans raise the limits.

articles.title: Mute, block, archive or clear a chat
articles.answer: Open the chat and use the menu at the top right: mute stops its notifications, block stops messages and calls both ways, archive moves it out of the list, and clear empties it for you only. “Report user” in the same menu tells the Connect2Minds team.

highlight.text: The chat menu (open a chat first).

articles.title: Voice and video calls
articles.answer: In a one-to-one chat press the phone or camera button to call. During the call you can mute, turn the camera off and share your screen. Teams have voice rooms and group calls in channels.

highlight.text: Voice call (open a chat first).
Video call.

articles.title: Use the site during a call
articles.answer: While you are in a call, opening any other section shows it inside the call page, so the call never drops. Use the floating call bar to mute, hang up, go back to the call or switch to side by side; in a video call you can pop the video out into a small window in Chrome or Edge.

articles.title: My Teams (workspaces)
articles.answer: My Teams is your team's workspace: text channels for chat (with replies, reactions, pins and search), voice rooms you can drop into, shared resources and members with roles. Create a team from the plus on the left.

highlight.text: Your teams; the plus creates a new one.
Text channels of the open team.

articles.title: Voice rooms in teams
articles.answer: Click a voice room in your team's sidebar to join it; everyone in the room can talk, turn on video or share a screen. You can also start a call inside any text channel with the phone or camera button.

highlight.text: Click a voice room to join.

articles.title: Plan together during a call
articles.answer: In a team call press Plan together: Project Hub opens beside the call. “Ask everyone” invites the others in the call to open it too, and you see who is looking at which tool.

articles.title: Project Hub
articles.answer: Project Hub plans a team's project. Plan: Board, List, Calendar, Timeline, Sprints. Define: Brief, Risks & decisions, Roles & workload. Track: Dashboard and Time. Together: Docs & meetings, Brainstorm, Canvas and Integrations. Everything updates live for your team.

highlight.text: All the planning tools, in four groups.

articles.title: Task board
articles.answer: The Board has four columns: To Do, In Progress, Review and Done. Drag cards between them, filter by tag or person and click a card to open everything about the task.

highlight.text: Drag cards between columns; click one to open it.

articles.title: Task details, checklist and comments
articles.answer: Click any task to open its panel: status, assignee, sprint, start and due dates, estimate, a checklist, the tasks it waits for, comments (type @ to mention someone, attach files), a timer and its history. Everything saves as you change it.

articles.title: List view and bulk editing
articles.answer: List shows every task as a table you can search, filter and sort. Tick several to change their status, assignee, sprint or priority at once, and export to CSV.

highlight.text: Open List.

articles.title: Calendar of due dates
articles.answer: Calendar shows tasks on their due dates by month. Drag a task to another day to move it; tasks without a date wait on the side until you drag them in.

articles.title: Timeline (Gantt chart)
articles.answer: Timeline draws each task as a bar from start to due date, with milestones as diamonds and arrows for what waits for what. Drag a bar to move it, drag its ends to change the dates; conflicts are marked in red.

highlight.text: Open Timeline.

articles.title: Sprints and backlog
articles.answer: A sprint is a short stretch of work with a goal. Create sprints, drag tasks from the backlog into them, start one, and when you finish it the unfinished tasks move to the next sprint or back to the backlog.

articles.title: Project brief
articles.answer: The Brief is one page your team agrees on: the problem, who it is for, goals, what is in and out of scope, deliverables, how success is measured and the deadline (with a countdown).

articles.title: Risks and decisions
articles.answer: Write down what could go wrong with its likelihood, impact, owner and plan; the grid shows the riskiest first. The decision log records what was decided, why and by whom.

articles.title: Roles (RACI) and workload
articles.answer: Roles & workload shows each person's open and late tasks, estimated and logged hours, and flags anyone overloaded. The RACI table says who is Responsible, Accountable, Consulted and Informed for each area.

articles.title: Project dashboard
articles.answer: The Dashboard shows how much is done, what is late or waiting, hours this week, the next milestone, tasks by stage and a burndown chart for the running sprint.

articles.title: Time tracking
articles.answer: Start a timer from any task (one runs at a time and shows in the header), or log hours by hand. The Time tool totals hours per person, per task and per day, and exports them.

articles.title: Docs and meeting notes
articles.answer: Docs & meetings holds shared pages written in simple formatting (headings, lists, checkboxes, links, tables) and meeting notes with attendees, agenda and action items that become tasks with one click.

articles.title: Brainstorm and mind map
articles.answer: Brainstorm has sticky notes in columns that everyone can vote on; the best become tasks with one click. Mind map grows a tree of ideas: select a node and press Tab for a child, Enter for a sibling, F2 to rename.

articles.title: Planning canvas
articles.answer: The Canvas is your team's shared whiteboard. Draw with the pen and highlighter, add shapes (rectangle, ellipse, diamond, triangle, hexagon, star, speech bubble, database), sticky notes, text, pictures and frames, and join shapes with arrows that stay attached. Everything saves by itself and teammates see your cursor and changes live. Press ? on the canvas for every shortcut.

highlight.text: Every drawing tool. Each has a one-key shortcut.

articles.title: Drawing on the canvas
articles.answer: Pick a tool on the left: P pen, M highlighter, E eraser (drag across what you want gone), R/O/D for shapes (the small arrow on the shape button shows all nine), T text, N sticky note. Select something to get the style bar: colour, fill, stroke width and style, opacity, text size, alignment, plus front/back, group, align, lock, duplicate and delete. Ctrl+Z undoes and Ctrl+Shift+Z redoes. Hold Shift for squares, circles and 45° lines; Alt stops snapping.

highlight.text: Pen, highlighter, eraser and shapes are here.

articles.title: Connecting shapes
articles.answer: Pick the arrow (A) and drag from one shape to another: both ends stay attached, so the arrow follows when you move the shapes. The small arrow on the line button gives a straight line, an elbow connector and a curved one; the style bar changes the arrowheads. Double-click an arrow to give it a label such as Yes or No.

highlight.text: Arrows, lines, elbow and curved connectors.

articles.title: Frames and present mode
articles.answer: Draw a frame (F) round each part of your board. Present shows the frames one after another in full screen: use the arrow keys or Space, Esc to stop. Number frame names (1 Problem, 2 Idea) to set the order. Teammates on the canvas get a Follow button so their view moves with your slides, and the laser pointer (K) shows them where to look.

highlight.text: Start presenting your frames.

articles.title: Pictures, templates and tasks on the canvas
articles.answer: Paste a picture, drop it on the board or press I to add one; only your workspace can see it. Templates adds a ready starter (flowchart, SWOT, user journey, system design, retro, impact vs effort, weekly plan). Select a sticky note and use the task button in the style bar to turn it into a Project Hub task; the note then shows whether the task is to do, in progress or done.

highlight.text: Ready-made starters.

articles.title: Saving, versions and export
articles.answer: The canvas saves by itself, and two people drawing at once both keep their work. File → Version history keeps the canvas every 10 minutes while people draw and always before it is cleared or replaced (the last 30), and restores any of them. File also exports PNG, SVG or a PDF with one page per frame, copies the board as a picture, and can export only what you selected.

highlight.text: Export, copy and version history.

articles.title: GitHub and Figma links
articles.answer: Link your team's public GitHub repository to see its pull requests and commits, and a Figma file to see it inside Project Hub.

articles.title: Project templates
articles.answer: Admins of a workspace can start from a template: College project, Hackathon, Startup MVP or Research paper. It adds a brief, sprints, dated tasks with milestones, risks and a starter page. Press Templates under the board's name.

articles.title: College Hub
articles.answer: College Hub connects a college's students with their approved teachers: notices and activities, groups formed for activities, college and class chat rooms, a calendar, shared resources, Q&A and attendance. Work handed in and marks are here too.

highlight.text: The sections of College Hub.

articles.title: Groups for college activities
articles.answer: When a teacher posts an activity, form or join a group under Groups (if students may form groups), choose a topic, hand in work before the deadline and do the weekly check-ins.

articles.title: Ask doubts (College Q&A)
articles.answer: Ask a question in College Hub's Q&A; classmates and teachers answer and vote, and the asker can mark the best answer. You can ask anonymously: only teachers see who asked.

articles.title: Become a teacher on College Hub
articles.answer: Teachers apply from Apply as teacher in the account menu: a short form with proof that you teach at the college. After approval you can post notices, manage groups, take attendance and give marks.

articles.title: Become a verification admin
articles.answer: College staff can apply as admin from the account menu to verify students' ID cards for their departments. The founder reviews each application.

articles.title: My Study
articles.answer: My Study keeps your timetable, attendance, a planner for assignments and exams, grades with your CGPA and a study timer. Today shows your classes and what is due.

highlight.text: Today, Timetable, Attendance, Planner, Grades and Timer.

articles.title: Set up your timetable
articles.answer: In My Study → Timetable add your subjects and their weekly classes. If a teacher published your class timetable, import it in one press.

highlight.text: Open Timetable.

articles.title: Track attendance
keywords: how many classes can i miss
articles.answer: In My Study → Attendance tap present or absent for each class. It shows your percentage per subject, how many classes you can still miss, or how many you must attend to get back to your goal (75% by default).

highlight.text: Open Attendance.

articles.title: Planner for assignments and exams
articles.answer: My Study → Planner holds your assignments, exams and to-dos with due dates. You get a reminder the evening before something is due.

highlight.text: Open Planner.

articles.title: Grades and CGPA
articles.answer: My Study → Grades works out your SGPA and CGPA from each semester's subjects, credits and grades (O, A+, A … on the 10-point scale), and what you need for a target CGPA.

highlight.text: Open Grades.

articles.title: Study timer and streak
articles.answer: My Study → Timer runs focus sessions (Pomodoro style) and counts your study minutes per subject and your daily streak.

highlight.text: Open Timer.

articles.title: Notes and past papers
articles.answer: Notes and papers is where students share notes and previous-year papers. Search by subject or college, vote and save the useful ones, share your own file, and report anything wrong.

highlight.text: Search by subject or college.

articles.title: Daily practice
articles.answer: Daily practice gives one aptitude and one coding question every day. Answer to keep your streak and earn points (10 for right, 2 for trying); you can catch up on the last 14 days and see your college's leaderboard.

highlight.text: Today's two questions.

articles.title: Resume builder
articles.answer: The Resume builder fills a one-page resume from your profile and projects. Edit it on the left, choose Classic or Modern, and Download PDF. It saves by itself.

highlight.text: Edit here; the page updates on the right.

articles.title: Research Collab
articles.answer: Research Collab collects sources for a topic from Wikipedia, OpenAlex and Crossref into one report you can save and share. It gathers sources; it does not write the research for you.

highlight.text: Type a topic and press Go.

articles.title: Activity history
articles.answer: Activity history lists what you did on the site by category, which you can search, export or clear. Open it from the menu under your picture.

articles.title: Plans and prices
articles.answer: Free gives every daily study tool and the basics of networking. **Student Pro** (₹99 a month or ₹799 a year) adds 60 AI tutor questions a day, AI flashcards and quizzes, unlimited mock tests with the full report and streak freezes, plus more outreach. The **Exam Pass** is ₹49 once for 30 days of the study perks. Networking Premium and Premium Plus add unlimited messaging, introductions and a profile boost. See **Plans**.

highlight.text: Personal and business plans.

articles.title: Billing and receipts
articles.answer: Plans & billing shows your plan, when it ends and your receipts. Payments go through Razorpay; plans don't renew by themselves, so renew with one click. For a refund write to Support within 7 days.

articles.title: Recruiter search
articles.answer: Recruiters on a paid plan search verified students by skill, college and GitHub activity, shortlist them and unlock contact details only for people who allow it.

articles.title: For colleges
articles.answer: Colleges get a free 60-day trial when their first teacher is approved, then an institution licence for attendance, handing in work, marks and analytics. Use “Talk to us” on the Plans page.

articles.title: Sponsor a challenge
articles.answer: Companies can sponsor challenges and hackathons on the Opportunities board with a sponsor plan. Ask from the Plans page (Sponsors tab).

articles.title: Delete my account
articles.answer: Open Account & privacy from the menu under your picture. Deleting logs you out everywhere and hides you at once; after 14 days everything personal is erased. Logging in before then cancels it. Messages and posts others rely on stay as “Deleted user”.

highlight.text: Delete my account is here.

articles.title: Download my data
articles.answer: Account & privacy has Download my data: one file with your profile and everything linked to your account. Your password and ID photo are never included.

highlight.text: Download a copy of your data.

articles.title: Privacy
articles.answer: Logged-in members see your profile card (not your email, roll number or ID photo). Messages are only between the people in them. The privacy page explains everything that is stored and your choices.

articles.title: Your data rights (DPDP Act 2023)
articles.answer: Under India's Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023 you can see what we hold (Download my data), correct it (edit your profile), erase it (Delete my account), withdraw consent, name a nominee on Account & privacy, and complain to our Grievance Officer, who replies within 90 days. If you are not satisfied you can then go to the Data Protection Board of India. The DPDP Act page explains each right and has the request form.

highlight.text: Send a data-rights request to the Grievance Officer here.

articles.title: Cookies and cookie settings
articles.answer: Essential cookies keep you logged in. With your OK the site also remembers your settings on this device (preferences) and counts visits with its own counter (visit counts, no IP address). Change your choice any time with Cookie settings on the Cookies page, linked at the bottom of every page.

highlight.text: Change what this device may keep here.

articles.title: Terms and honour code
articles.answer: Be respectful, do your own work, share only what you may share, be honest in teams, and no spam or scams. The terms page has the full rules and how paid plans work.

articles.title: Contact support
articles.answer: Use the Support page: pick a topic, describe what happened and leave an email for the reply. It goes straight to the Connect2Minds team.

highlight.text: Describe the problem here.

articles.title: Using it on a phone
articles.answer: The site works in your phone's browser. The bar at the bottom jumps between Home, Study, Discover, Messages and Me. You can add it to your home screen from the browser menu.

articles.title: Follow someone
articles.answer: Press Follow on anyone's card or profile. There are no friend requests; they see that you follow them and can follow you back.

articles.title: The bell
articles.answer: The bell at the top lists mentions, follows, profile views, College Hub news and more. Click one to open it; they are marked read when you open the list.

articles.title: Log out
articles.answer: Open the menu under your picture at the top right and press Log out. It also stops notifications on that device.

articles.title: Take the tour
articles.answer: I can walk you through the main parts of the site, one highlight at a time. Press “Start the tour”.

articles.title: Talking to this helper
articles.answer: Press the microphone in this panel and speak; switch on “Read answers aloud” to hear replies. Voice works in Chrome, Edge and Safari. You can also just type.

articles.title: Report a person, message or post
articles.answer: Press Report on a profile (under the Message and Follow buttons), the flag on a message in Messages, Teams or College Hub, the flag on an opportunity, or “Report this team” in team settings. Pick what is wrong and send. We acknowledge every report within 24 hours, decide within 15 days and tell you the result in your notifications. Only our team sees who reported. If someone is in danger, call 112.

articles.title: Change my password or log out other devices
articles.answer: Open Account & privacy from the menu under your picture. In “Password and devices” press Change password (you need the current one), or “Log out of all other devices” if you think someone else is using your account. Both keep this device logged in.

highlight.text: Change your password or log out other devices here.

articles.title: Two-step login (authenticator app)
articles.answer: Two-step login asks for a 6-digit code from an authenticator app after your password. Turn it on in Account & privacy: type your password, scan the QR code with Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator or Authy, type the code, then save the 10 backup codes. Lost your phone? Log in with a backup code, then turn two-step login off and on again.

highlight.text: Turn two-step login on here.

articles.title: Confirm my email address
articles.answer: In Account & privacy, the Email address card sends a 6-digit code to your email; type it there to confirm. “Use another email” changes the address the same way. A confirmed college email (.edu.in or .ac.in) also verifies a waiting student account.

highlight.text: Send yourself a code here.

articles.title: Age, under 18 and parent consent
articles.answer: Connect2Minds is for people aged 13 and over. Sign-up asks your date of birth; if you are under 18 you also give a parent's or guardian's email and we send them a link to agree, as India's DPDP Act requires. Until they agree your account is hidden and you cannot post or message; if they say no, the account is erased. We never count children's visits and recruiters cannot find them.

highlight.text: How children's data is handled.

articles.title: Refunds and cancelling a plan
articles.answer: Plans never renew by themselves, so there is nothing to cancel to stop charges; a plan simply ends on its date. You can get a refund within 7 days of paying if you have not used the paid features, and always if you were charged twice or the plan never switched on. Write to Support with the receipt number; approved refunds reach your card, UPI or bank in 5 to 7 working days.

articles.title: Contact Connect2Minds
articles.answer: The Contact us page lists the business name, address, email and phone, and the Grievance Officer for complaints about content, the service, payments or your data. For help with your account the Support form is quickest.

highlight.text: The Grievance Officer for complaints.

articles.title: Copyright and taking down my work
articles.answer: If your work was posted without permission, send the takedown form on the Copyright page: where it is, what your work is, and a good-faith statement. We acknowledge within 24 hours and remove complete requests within 36 hours. If your post was taken down by mistake, appeal through Support.

highlight.text: Send a takedown request here.

articles.title: What can this helper do?
articles.answer: Ask me how anything on the site works and I'll explain and take you there. I can also tell you what's due this week, your attendance, unread messages and find people by skill, add a planner task, mark attendance, or start a timer, always asking before I change anything.

articles.title: XP, daily goal and streak
articles.answer: Everything you study earns XP: daily questions, focus minutes, flashcards, tests, quizzes and helping your class. Reach your daily goal (you pick 10, 30, 50 or 80 XP on **Your progress**) to keep your streak. With Student Pro or the Exam Pass, 2 streak freezes a month cover a missed day by themselves.

highlight.text: Today's XP against your goal, and your streak.

articles.title: Exam Prep: syllabus units
articles.answer: **Exam Prep** keeps your subjects with their syllabus. Pick your class's syllabus (or paste it in once for everyone), set the exam date, and mark each unit To do, Learning, Revised or Confident. It tells you the daily pace to finish before the exam.

highlight.text: Your subjects, cards to review and the next exam.

articles.title: Flashcards and daily review
articles.answer: Make flashcard decks in **Exam Prep** (one at a time or paste many with | between front and back), or follow decks your class shares. Review every day: cards you find hard come back sooner, easy ones later. Each card reviewed earns 1 XP.

highlight.text: Start today's review from here.

articles.title: Past-paper questions
articles.answer: In a subject's **Past-paper questions** tab, add questions from previous-year papers with the year. When a question was asked in several years it moves to the top, so the class knows what to prepare first. From a past paper in Notes, use 'Add its questions to Exam Prep'.

highlight.text: Open a subject, then its Past-paper questions tab.

articles.title: AI Tutor
articles.answer: The **AI Tutor** answers doubts, writes 2- to 15-mark exam answers in the format universities expect, explains past-paper questions, and makes flashcards or a quiz from a unit or topic. Free accounts get 5 questions and 1 deck or quiz a day; Student Pro and the Exam Pass give 60 questions and 10 decks or quizzes a day, and can read your note files.

highlight.text: Pick a mode: doubt, exam answer, flashcards or quiz.

articles.title: Mock tests
articles.answer: **Mock tests** are timed aptitude and CS tests, from 15 to 55 questions, with every answer explained. Answers save as you pick them and the clock is the server's. Free accounts get one timed test a week; untimed topic practice is free and unlimited. Student Pro and the Exam Pass give unlimited tests plus a report of weak topics and time per question.

highlight.text: Pick a topic test or a placement round.

articles.title: Study rooms
articles.answer: In **Study rooms** you study alongside classmates on one shared timer, with no camera and no chat. Open a room (share its code) or join one from your college. A focus round you take part in counts for your XP and streak.

highlight.text: Open a room or join one.

articles.title: Weekly league
articles.answer: Every week the XP you earn puts you in your college's league (and one with the people you follow), on **Your progress**. It starts again each Monday; the top three get a badge on their profile and everyone is told their place.

highlight.text: This week's league.

articles.title: Exam Pass
articles.answer: The **Exam Pass** is one ₹49 payment for 30 days of every study perk: 60 AI tutor questions a day, AI flashcards and quizzes, unlimited mock tests with the full report, and streak freezes. It does not renew; it simply ends. Networking limits stay as on the free plan.

highlight.text: The Exam Pass is at the top.

articles.title: Find events
articles.answer: Open Events in the top bar. Upcoming shows what your college and others have planned; switch to the calendar view, search, or filter by type, date and seats. Save an event with the bookmark to get a reminder before registration closes.

highlight.text: Upcoming, happening now, past, and your own events.
Search by title, host, tag or college.

articles.title: Register for an event
articles.answer: Open the event and press Register. Your name and college are filled in from your profile; answer the organiser's questions and agree to share your details with them. If the event is full you join the waitlist and move up automatically when a seat opens. You can cancel from the event page until shortly before the start.

highlight.text: Open any event to register.

articles.title: Your event ticket and QR code
articles.answer: Your tickets are in My events. Open one and show its QR code at the entrance. The ticket is saved on your phone, so it opens without internet. If someone got a screenshot of it, press New code: the old one stops working.

highlight.text: Upcoming shows your tickets.

articles.title: Create an event
articles.answer: Choose Events, then Create an event. Pick a template, fill in the six steps (it saves as you go) and submit. Teachers publish at once. A student's event goes to a teacher of their college first; a public one also to the college admin. You must be a verified student, a teacher or a professional to create events.

highlight.text: Start from a template or copy an earlier event.

articles.title: Run your event: registrations, announcements, staff
articles.answer: My events, Organising, opens each event's dashboard: who registered (approve, waitlist, download a CSV), announcements to everyone or to one group, volunteers and managers, certificates, and an activity log of every change and download.

highlight.text: Organising lists the events you run.

articles.title: Check people in at the door
articles.answer: Open the event dashboard and press Scanner (volunteers go straight there). Point the camera at tickets; a green screen means let them in, red says why not, including tickets already used. Search by name works too. Without internet the scans are kept and sent later; the printed attendance sheet is the backup.

highlight.text: Open an event you organise, then the Scanner.

articles.title: Event certificates
articles.answer: Everyone checked in at an event gets a participation certificate with a code like C2M-ABCD-EFGH. Find and print yours in My events, Certificates, and choose whether it shows on your profile. Anyone can check a certificate on the certificate check page.

highlight.text: Type or scan a certificate code here.

articles.title: Approve student events (teachers)
articles.answer: Teachers find student events and club requests in College Hub, Events. Approve, ask for changes or reject, always with a note the student sees. Bigger changes to a live event (date, place, seats) come back here too. Home reminds you when something is waiting.

highlight.text: The Events tab is shown to teachers.

articles.title: Clubs and departments as event hosts
articles.answer: A host is the department, club or company behind events. Create one from the event wizard's Host field; a teacher's host is live at once, a student's is approved by a teacher. Follow a host to hear about its new events.

highlight.text: Name the host and add a logo.
